s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of purpuric lesions with systemic involvement and multi-organ dysfunction
salient_findings: Purpuric lesions on face, elbows, knees, and feet
Skin sloughing off lesions on elbows and knees
Reticulated purpuric macules and patches on extensor surfaces
Dusky purpuric macules and patches on nose, cheeks, forehead, and ear
Hypercalcemia and acute kidney injury
Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses
Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 80s
History of nonischemic cardiomyopathy and chronic kidney disease
Presented with altered mental status after an unwitnessed fall
Purpuric lesions developed on nose, ear, and extensor surfaces of arms
Laboratory tests showed hypercalcemia and acute kidney injury
Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear
Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses
Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis
Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels
Biopsy findings showed intravascular fibrinoid material with cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi
CT scan of pelvis revealed lytic bony lesions
Bone marrow biopsy showed hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction

shortlist.label: Cryoglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has elevated serum cryoglobulin levels and biopsy findings showing intravascular fibrinoid material with cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has hypercalcemia, acute kidney injury, and bone marrow biopsy showing hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction

shortlist.label: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis and abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses

shortlist.label: Light-chain amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has hypercalcemia, acute kidney injury, and bone marrow biopsy showing hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction

shortlist.label: Plasma cell dyscrasia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has bone marrow biopsy showing hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction, and abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses

raw.rationale: The presence of hypercalcemia, lytic bony lesions on CT scan, and a bone marrow biopsy showing 80% plasma cells with κ-light-chain restriction are highly suggestive of multiple myeloma. Additionally, the abnormal paraprotein band and monoclonal IgG-κ protein support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cryoglobulinemia
rejected.why: While cryoglobulinemia is present, it is likely a secondary phenomenon related to the underlying plasma cell dyscrasia, rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with IgM monoclonal protein, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Light-chain amyloidosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of amyloid deposits on biopsy, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Plasma cell dyscrasia
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes multiple myeloma, but multiple myeloma is a more specific diagnosis that better explains the patient's findings.
